DTR · TALK ABOUT A SCENE

Lettuce for Congress

STS-HS12-L4-13001400-HSCE-ARA-API-01 • HS Civics and Economics Grade 12 • Campaigns for National, State, and Local Elective Offices
Look at the picture. You will answer some questions about it. Press the play button to hear each question. Record your answer for each question. You can listen to your answer and record it again. Click SUBMIT RECORDINGS when you have answered all the questions.
JUST FOR FUN · OPTIONAL
Dalip Singh Saund came from Punjab, India, and grew lettuce in California's Imperial Valley, but for more than twenty-five years the law would not let him become a citizen. He finally became one in 1949, and in 1956 he ran for Congress with very little money. His opponent flew her own airplane from one campaign stop to the next and threw a barbecue with famous guests, yet Saund won and became the first Asian American elected to Congress. Tonight, Simran, Arjun, and Tala are studying the objects in their exhibit to tell his story.
If your campaign had very little money, how would you reach voters who live far apart on farms?
Optional. You do not have to record this one.
1
What is Simran doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what Simran is doing with exact evidence. Use precise words, not "looking at stuff."
2
What is Arjun holding?
Look at the picture. Justify what Arjun holds and why its date matters. Compare it with the other year you see.
3
What is the teacher doing?
Look at the picture. Justify what the teacher is doing and how it helps the truck reach voters. Name the object exactly.
4
What place is this? How do you know?
Look at the picture. Justify what place this is with at least two exact clues.
5
Tell me about the truck.
Look at the picture. Justify what the truck is for with at least two exact details. Use exact nouns.
6
What is Tala wearing?
Look at the picture. Justify Tala's role from her clothing and what she is doing. Be precise.
Record an answer for each question, then submit.
